source.rule: Copyrighted sources may remain external; expected SHA-256 must be retained.

evidence.rule: Execution alone never promotes evidence status.

comparison.rule: Reference population and evidence boundary must be explicit.

discrepancy.rule: Do not hide or tune unresolved discrepancies.

verification.rule: Computational verification is not engineering qualification.

reproduction.study_override: verification_tolerance {rel, abs, purpose, statement, rationale, rounding_guards}

verification.non_mutation_rule: Verification must not mutate the evidence being verified. Recompute in isolation and compare with frozen evidence; regeneration is a separate explicit operation.
verification.tolerance_rule: Verification tolerances define recomputation equivalence only; they are not engineering acceptance or validation tolerances.

ingestion.rule: Ingestion discovers candidates only; no candidate becomes engineering evidence without review and reproduction.

source_fingerprint.rule: Persist basename/hash/metadata only; never persist machine-specific absolute source paths.

target_candidates.rule: Lexical figure/table/equation discovery is a review queue, not evidence.

promotion_gate.rule: A study cannot enter the live registry while DRAFT/BLOCKED or without targets, results, tests and callable tools.

source_map.rule: Persist page-level hashes/counts and bounded target excerpts only; never persist full extracted source text by default.

target_dossiers.rule: Target dossiers are source-location aids. Automated excerpts/symbol/unit candidates require review before evidence promotion.

reproduction_tasks.rule: Generated tasks are plans, not completed reproduction or verification evidence.

structure_candidates.rule: Structure extraction is heuristic review material; extracted blocks/rows/captions do not become engineering evidence automatically.

comparison_templates.rule: Comparison templates specify candidate metrics only; metrics require source-backed reproduced/reference populations before evaluation.

discrepancy_assessment.rule: Classification controls review/escalation workflow only; it cannot decide physical acceptability or engineering qualification.

discrepancy_gate.rule: Unresolved high-priority evidence conflicts block new-study promotion until resolved, bounded, or explicitly accepted by documented decision.

discrepancy_taxonomy.rule: A taxonomy label describes the kind of discrepancy and where it was established. It never changes an observation, value, status, decision or qualification, and it does not state a cause.
discrepancy_taxonomy.decision_order_rule: Apply the categories in decision_order; the first whose decision_rule holds is the category. Exactly one category per discrepancy.

MODEL_VS_EXPERIMENT_GAP.definition: A model prediction (published or reproduced) differs from measured experimental data reported in the source.
MODEL_VS_EXPERIMENT_GAP.decision_rule: Use when one side of the comparison is a physical measurement. Takes precedence over all other categories.
MODEL_VS_EXPERIMENT_GAP.not_this_when: Both sides are calculations or printed values.

MODEL_FORM_DIFFERENCE.definition: Two models, each implemented as published, give different results because of their stated assumptions, kinematics or idealisations.
MODEL_FORM_DIFFERENCE.decision_rule: Use when both models are reproduced or taken as published and the difference is attributable to the stated model form, not to a printed value.
MODEL_FORM_DIFFERENCE.not_this_when: One side is a printed value that the other side contradicts; use NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.

MISSING_OR_INSUFFICIENT_SOURCE_INFORMATI.definition: The printed equations, parameters or load-case statements are insufficient to determine a published result uniquely, so a source-bounded implementation cannot reconcile with it.
MISSING_OR_INSUFFICIENT_SOURCE_INFORMATI.decision_rule: Use when the conflict disappears only by supplying information the source does not give. Do not supply it.
MISSING_OR_INSUFFICIENT_SOURCE_INFORMATI.not_this_when: The missing item is only a unit (UNIT_OR_DIMENSION) or a quantity definition (QUANTITY_DEFINITION_OR_CONVENTION).

UNIT_OR_DIMENSION.definition: A unit is missing, conflicts between source statements, or makes a stated value dimensionally or physically untenable, while the magnitudes are otherwise consistent under one unit reading.
UNIT_OR_DIMENSION.decision_rule: Use when the conflict is resolved by the choice of unit alone. Takes precedence over NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.
UNIT_OR_DIMENSION.not_this_when: The digits themselves disagree under any unit reading.

QUANTITY_DEFINITION_OR_CONVENTION.definition: The definition, sign, normalisation, amplitude or reference convention of a quantity (or of a quantitative claim) is ambiguous or used inconsistently; the numbers reconcile under one reading only.
QUANTITY_DEFINITION_OR_CONVENTION.decision_rule: Use when the printed numbers are reproduced under one stated reading and contradicted under another.

NOTATION_OR_TYPOGRAPHY.definition: A printed symbol, operator or equation text contradicts the surrounding text or neighbouring equations, without a conflicting numerical value.
NOTATION_OR_TYPOGRAPHY.decision_rule: Use when the contradiction is in notation only. No cause (typesetting, author error) is asserted.
NOTATION_OR_TYPOGRAPHY.not_this_when: A numerical value is affected; use NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.

PRECISION_OR_DIGITIZATION_RESIDUAL.definition: A difference between a published value and a reproduction that lies within, or is attributable to, the published rounding precision or the uncertainty of graphical digitization.
PRECISION_OR_DIGITIZATION_RESIDUAL.decision_rule: Use when the difference does not exceed the recorded rounding band or digitization uncertainty. Usually BOUNDED.
PRECISION_OR_DIGITIZATION_RESIDUAL.not_this_when: The difference exceeds the recorded band; use NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.

NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.definition: A printed numerical value disagrees, beyond its stated precision, with another source statement of the same quantity or with a source-bounded reproduction or independent check of it.
NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.decision_rule: Use when the same quantity has two incompatible values (printed vs printed, or printed vs recomputed).
NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.not_this_when: No other value of the same quantity exists and the conflict is only with physics; use PHYSICAL_IMPLAUSIBILITY.

PHYSICAL_IMPLAUSIBILITY.definition: A printed value or trend is contradicted by basic mechanics applied to other source data, while no other source statement gives a conflicting value of the same quantity.
PHYSICAL_IMPLAUSIBILITY.decision_rule: Use when the conflict is established only through physical bounds (equilibrium, buoyancy, material strength, weight support).
PHYSICAL_IMPLAUSIBILITY.not_this_when: Another printed or recomputed value of the same quantity exists; use NUMERICAL_VALUE_CONFLICT.

loci.WITHIN_SOURCE: Two or more statements of the source (paragraph, table, figure axis, caption, equation) disagree with each other.
loci.SOURCE_INCOMPLETE: A single source statement lacks information needed to interpret or reproduce it (e.g. a missing unit or parameter).
loci.SOURCE_VS_REPRODUCTION: A published value differs from EngiProof's PUBLISHED-class implementation of the source's own method.
loci.SOURCE_VS_INDEPENDENT: A published value differs from an INDEPENDENT-class check (different formulation, numerical method or measurement).
loci.SOURCE_VS_PHYSICAL_BOUNDS: The conflict is established by basic mechanics applied to other source data.
loci.MODEL_VS_MODEL: Two models, each as published, are compared.
loci.MODEL_VS_EXPERIMENT: A model is compared with measured data.

discrepancy_taxonomy.loci_rule: List every locus through which the discrepancy was established (one or more).
discrepancy_taxonomy.legacy_rule: Existing free-text classification_hint values are retained unchanged and are not mapped automatically. New discrepancies must use a taxonomy category or a listed legacy hint. Mapping legacy records to the taxonomy requires human review (engiproof/contracts/discrepancy_taxonomy_mapping.json).
